newsitem.title: SPAIN: INSTANT VIEW - Spanish March inflation.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Spanish March inflation.

text.p: The following are analysts' reactions to a 0.1 percent rise in Spain's Consumer Price Index (CPI) in March, for a 2.2 percent year-on-year rise, as announced by the National Statistics Institute INE on Friday.
In February, CPI rose 2.5 percent year on year.
ANTONIO MIGUELANEZ, ECONOMIST, BANCO BILBAO VIZCAYA, MADRID:

"Our initial valuation is positive, not just because it is below forecasts, but also because of the favourable performance of some components which are generally inflationary, such as housing and medicine,"

"Furthermore, foods have performed positively despite the rise in the price of tobacco in March. We're in a good position to see new falls in the next few months and in principle that leads us to think that the CPI may break the two percent barrier in May...there's margin for a key rate cut,"
ANTONIO VILLARROYA, ECONOMIST AT MERRILL LYNCH IN MADRID

"It's a good figure, particularly as regards fresh food prices (which fell 0.9 percent from February). There's still resistance for goods and services prices to go down. We'll have to wait and see the effects of the liberalisation measures approved by the government.

As regards the Bank of Spain, it's clear it has room to cut rates by 25 basis points in the next month and whether or not it cuts next week will depend on market expectations and the position of the peseta."
JUAN ANTONIO MIELGO, ECONOMIST AT BANK OF AMERICA IN MADRID

"These are really good data, both the headline and the core rate, as well as processed food (unchanged from February)...I think that from here to April 15 those who didn't think there'd be a rate cut will start to anticipate a 25 basis point move, and those who were expecting 25 basis points will start to expect a 50 basis point cut."
